Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Church life

save verb

from danger or harm

also rescue, save a life, saviour

classical

Hor. S. 1.9.78: sīc mē servāvit Apollō
Traupman 262, 374

servō, servāre, servāvī, servātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive; from something, ab or ex and the ablative

save, keep safe

Other words

  • cōnservō, cōnservāre, cōnservāvī, cōnservātum — save, spare, keep unharmed

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Caes. BG 2.15 (Lewis & Short): Caesar sēsē eōs cōnservātūrum dīxit

  • ēripiō, ēripere, ēripuī, ēreptum — rescue, snatch from (danger)

    verb, third conjugation (-iō); with ex or ab and the ablative, or the dative · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.53 (Lewis & Short): ē manibus hostium; Traupman 370

  • salvō, salvāre, salvāvī, salvātum — save (in Christian Latin)

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · late Latin · Vulg. Mt. 8.25: Domine, salvā nōs: perīmus.; M-O s.v. save (eccl.)

    (vōx Latīnitātis ecclēsiasticae: Vulg., Hier.)

    Late Latin (Lewis & Short). The Vulgate also says salvum facere: Domine, salvum mē fac (Mt. 14.30).

  • salvātor, salvātōris m. — saviour

    noun, third declension · also used · late Latin · Vulg. Is. 12.3: dē fontibus salvātōris

    (vōx Latīnitātis ecclēsiasticae: Vulg.)

    Lewis & Short: late Latin; the classical word is servātor.

Examples

  • sīc mē servāvit Apollō

    So Apollo saved me.Hor. S. 1.9.78

  • Dī mē servant, salva rēs est.

    The gods are looking after me: all is well.Plaut. Aul. 207

  • Domine, salvā nōs: perīmus.

    Lord, save us: we are perishing.Vulg. Mt. 8.25

See also protect, help, save.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
